label: prop:plancherel-term-7-formulation
title: Universal residue at curvature-rank $k \geq 4$ (Molien-weighted log functional)
html:
Define the curvature-rank-k residue functional using the Molien (fake-degree) weight

  w_\lambda(q) \;=\; \frac{f^\lambda \, q^{-\kappa_\lambda} \, \dim_q V_\lambda}{[n]_q!},
  \qquad
  \kappa_\lambda \;=\; \sum_{\square \in \lambda} c(\square)
  \;=\; n(\lambda') - n(\lambda),

where f^\lambda is the number of standard Young tableaux (the classical Wedderburn block dimension), c(\square) = j - i is the content of the box in row i, column j, and \lambda' is the conjugate partition:

  \Phi_k(\mathcal{K}, \mathcal{T})
  \;:=\; \sum_{\substack{\lambda \,\vdash\, n \\ \mathrm{depth}(\lambda) = k}}
  w_\lambda(q) \cdot \log\Bigl|\!\int_{A_\lambda}\! \rho(\beta_\mathcal{K}) \cdot \mathcal{T}\Bigr|.

The universal residue extracts the high-tower contribution as:

  \mathfrak{m}^{\geq 4}_{q,\mathcal{K}}(\mathcal{T})
  \;=\; \alpha \cdot \!\!\sum_{k \geq 4}\!\Phi_k(\mathcal{K}, \mathcal{T}),
  \qquad \alpha \;=\; m_e \cdot 8G.

At low strata (k \leq 3), the restricted Frobenius integral routes through distinct hyperbolic-knot ideals. At deep strata (k \geq 4), specific knot identities evaporate. The surviving residue isolates the universal Frobenius co-Casimir tail, dependent solely on the block weight topology.

On the choice of weight family. The functional was formerly defined against \dim_q^2 V_\lambda/[n]_q!. The replacement is not a change of normalisation: the two weights differ by up to a factor 1831 per partition at n = 9, which is A = 3. Three properties distinguish the Molien weight.

Three objects carry the name "Molien" in the corpus, and only the first two are used here. (i) The fake-degree identity \sum_\lambda f^\lambda q^{-\kappa_\lambda}\dim_q(\lambda) = [n]_q!. (ii) The Molien weight f^\lambda q^{-\kappa_\lambda}\dim_q(\lambda)/[n]_q!, the measure that identity normalises. (iii) The two-variable Molien series M_\nu(u,t) attached to the Jones–Markov traces at n = 3 and n = 4, a generating function and not a weight on partitions.

  1. It is the weight of the symmetrising trace. Every Markov trace on H_n(q) yields weights with \sum_\lambda f^\lambda y_\lambda(z) = 1 (proved directly at n = 4), so being normalised does not single the Molien weight out. What does is that it is the weight of the z = 0 trace, the symmetrising trace \tau(T_w) = \delta_{w,1}: the Ocneanu weight at z = 0 coincides with the Molien weight, and its normalisation is \tau(1) = 1. Classically, q^{-\kappa_\lambda}\dim_q(\lambda) = q^{-n(n-1)/2}R_\lambda(q^2) with R_\lambda the fake degree, so the identity (i) is Steinberg's theorem on the graded coinvariant algebra of S_n [steinberg1964]. The alternative \dim_q^2/D^2 is normalised by dividing by D^2 = \sum_\mu \dim_q^2, i.e. by construction.
  2. The exponent \kappa_\lambda is forced, not chosen. In the family f^\lambda q^{c\kappa_\lambda}\dim_q/[n]_q! with c real, normalisation already at n = 2 reads (q^c + q^{-c})/(q + q^{-1}) = 1, which for q > 1 forces c = \pm 1. The two signs are one measure read on transposed diagrams: conjugation fixes f^\lambda and the hook multiset and negates \kappa.
  3. It is the literature's q-Plancherel measure. f^\lambda q^{-\kappa_\lambda}\dim_q(\lambda)/[n]_q! = \mathbb{M}_{n,q^2}(\lambda) for every n, every partition and every q: substituting Q = q^2 into \mathbb{M}_{n,Q}(\lambda) = Q^{n(\lambda)}f^\lambda/\prod_x\{h(x)\}_Q and using \sum_x h(x) = n(\lambda) + n(\lambda') + n gives the left side exactly. So the Féray–Méliot asymptotics apply to this weight and to nothing else in the corpus. See Asymptotic skeleton of the q-Plancherel measure \mathbb{M}_{n,q}.

Molien within the Wenzl family. The z = q^3/(q^2+1) Markov trace and the colour trace are the Wenzl levels r = 2 and r = 3; the Molien weight is the z = 0 member of the same Ocneanu family, its r \to \infty end. A finite level carries a row cap, and \Phi_k for k \geq 3 is non-zero only at the Molien end. The choice of Molien therefore rests on its being the uncapped member of the family, not on the +21.4\% gain reported below.

The former weight is n-dependent, and n = 3A. c_n = \sum_\lambda \dim_q^2/[n]_q! is 0.9874 / 0.9911 / 1.1109 / 1.5171 at n = 3/6/9/12 at the substrate q_0, and the defect is structural rather than a q-integer-convention artifact — the q-deformation breaks Burnside's \sum_\lambda (f^\lambda)^2 = n!, and no convention restores it. Because \Phi_k is linear in w_\lambda, a \lambda-independent rescaling cancels from a ratio of two w-weighted sums at the same n and from nothing else. Two ways that fails, both of which occurred in production:

  1. Across n. Any quantity comparing different n — equivalently different mass number A — is distorted by the spread of c_n.
  2. At fixed n, against a non-w-weighted quantity. A w-weighted number compared to an experimental magnitude, a closed-form scalar, or a y_\lambda-weighted object does not cancel, because only one side carries c_n. Instances of this failure were measured in the deuteron f_{pn} weighting and in the Yekutieli volume join.

A same-n ratio is necessary for cancellation but not sufficient — the numerators must match too. This is the trap in the present migration and it is easy to get backwards. The six candidates of the n = 6 Wedderburn comparison are all ratios of w-weighted sums at fixed n = 6, so they are exactly invariant under \dim_q^2/[n]_q! \to \dim_q^2/D^2 — same numerator, \lambda-independent constant. They are not invariant under the move to Molien, whose numerator is \lambda-dependent relative to \dim_q^2.

The second arm is retained and labelled. The requirement set does not separate Molien from \dim_q^2/D^2 — it asks only that the normaliser be n-independent, and both satisfy that; both are legitimate probability measures. So both arms are computed and reported, Molien primary. They disagree: Molien ranks 5_2 best (+21.4\% against its own baseline, with 6_1 worse than baseline), while \dim_q^2/D^2 ranks 6_1 best (+1.7\%). Quoting one number would conceal that. Note the corpus's structural 6_1 naming comes from the GB-filtration route, which carries no weight family at all and is untouched by either arm.

Two further measures exist and are not arms here. The V^{\otimes n} Schur–Weyl share f^\lambda \prod[N+c]_q/[h]_q lives on partitions with at most N rows and is normalised by [N]_q^n — a different index set and normaliser, so not a rescaling of anything above; at N = 2 the \mathrm{SU}(N) row cap zeroes it on every partition with more than two rows, exactly as it zeroes y_\lambda. The classical (f^\lambda)^2/n! reached via \mathrm{End}(V^{\otimes n}) is Burnside-normalised at every n but is q-independent, so it could carry no substrate dependence into \Phi_k at all.

Two candidates are excluded outright, independently of the choice between the two that remain. The Markov weights y_\lambda of the canonical Frobenius pairing are scope-(b) excluded: the \mathrm{SU}(N) row cap sets y_\lambda = 0 on every stratum of depth \geq N, so \Phi_3 vanishes identically and all three candidate knots reproduce the no-FR baseline to the last digit. The historical \dim_q^2/[n]_q! is scope-(b) excluded for cross-nucleus use by the n-dependence above; it remains valid within a single n, where the normaliser cancels from any ratio of w-weighted sums.

One caution on citing the identity. The identity (i) is \sum_\lambda f^\lambda q^{-\kappa_\lambda} \dim_q(\lambda) = [n]_q! — the q^{-\kappa_\lambda} is part of it. A "Molien weight" written as f^\lambda\dim_q(\lambda) without that factor is a different object and is not normalised: with \dim_q in the balanced convention it sums to \approx 0.922 at n = 6 at q_0, and \approx 0.061 at q = 2, rather than 1. (In the fake-degree convention the power of q already sits inside \dim_q, and the plain sum is exactly 1: it is the same identity.)
